notes: Read by the workflow and interpreted only by workflows/code/route.js.
The contract is what validate-classification.js holds model output to. Output that fails it is CLASSIFICATION_FAILED and never reaches these rules.
Rules are tried in order; the first whose conditions all hold wins. Conditions compare `relevance` or `criteria.<name>` for equality and are ANDed.

Order is load-bearing. The two contradiction rules come first, so a contradiction is always labelled as one. `contradiction-not-relevant` must precede `not-relevant`, or output that calls a notice irrelevant while its own criteria say it is software in the target market would be dismissed with no human seeing it (docs/DESIGN-AMENDMENTS.md A2).
`contradiction-match-off-market`: a match verdict whose own criteria say the notice is outside the target market is two incompatible statements, not an uncertain one (A8).
`scope-unclear` precedes `not-relevant`, as in the design doc: an irrelevant verdict with unclear scope goes to review. Over-review is the safe direction.
`strong-match` requires a match verdict and all three criteria (A6). A rule may route to AUTO_MATCH or NOT_RELEVANT only when it requires the matching verdict; route.js refuses this file otherwise.
There is no `currently_open` criterion. merge-results.js removes closed notices before classification, so every notice the model reads is open by construction (A7).

`confidence_floor` applies only when the rule that fired would decide without a human. Below `min`, AUTO_MATCH and NOT_RELEVANT both become NEEDS_REVIEW, recorded as `below-confidence-floor`. Confidence only holds a notice back for a person; it never authorizes a route (A9).
Anything no rule matches falls back to NEEDS_REVIEW.

rules.basis: Design doc §6 and §7, amendments A6 and A7
